body.heading: Get comfortable
paragraphs: Choose a window where you can see trees, a garden, or the sky. Sit comfortably with your adult and your notebook.
You do not need to go anywhere special. Birds visit almost every street and garden if you are quiet and patient.

body.heading: Watch and draw
paragraphs: When a bird lands, look at its colours, its size, and the shape of its beak. Draw it quickly in your notebook before it flies away.
You do not need to know its name. Write what you saw instead, like “small brown bird with a red chest.” Your adult can help you look the name up later.

body.heading: Listen too
paragraphs: Close your eyes for a moment and just listen. Birds sing and call in different patterns. Can you copy one of the sounds?
Try watching at a different time of day. Morning visitors are often different from evening ones.

description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: sit quietly at a window and spot, draw, and listen to visiting birds.

safetyNotes: Watch wild birds from a distance and never try to touch them or their nests.
If you watch from outdoors, stay with your adult in a safe place away from roads.
screenFreeExtension: Put out a shallow dish of clean water for birds with your adult, then watch from inside to see who comes for a drink.
takeaway: Quiet watching turns an ordinary window into a front-row seat for nature.
